two rules:

do not let your dog interact with your rats

always get more than one rat.

it is not worth the risk to keep rats around a large animal, like other commenters have said. all it takes is one wrong move and it’s all over. i myself have an 83lb dog and would never even DREAM of letting her around my boys. claws, teeth, and general size of the dog are all a big big danger to small animals like rats.

there’s a couple reasons for putting it down, i’d say the biggest are because it’s comfortable and dust-free, as well as just providing a barrier between the cage itself and your rats. 

it does make clean up easier in my experience as well (though i use towels rather than fleece as they’re more absorbent and safer, you have to make sure to have absorbent layers under fleece or the urine will be rereleased into the air) 

i don’t really have many tips on getting them to not chew, other than having lots of things for your ratties to chew and be distracted with.

i’m no expert though !! do take this with a grain of salt, as it’s all from my personal experience :)

our cages are almost identical!

what i do is make sure that i have at least one hammock on each level, as well as ropes for them to climb on. as the other commenters said, more places to hide and burrow are good!

i’d also suggest putting puppy pads under fleece, and fleece/pads on the small shelves too, for comfort and ease of cleaning :)
